cues.zh: 我叫 Moxy Marlinspike，来自 Institute for Disruptive Studies。
cues.en: My name is Moxy Marlinspike, I am from the Institute for Disruptive Studies.

cues.zh: 嗯，我不太喜欢开场介绍，所以今天我想介绍两位朋友。
cues.en: Um, I don't really like introductions, so instead today, I'm going to introduce two friends of mine.

cues.zh: 嗯，Shane 和 Sarah，大概是我在这世上最喜欢的两个人。
cues.en: Um, Shane and Sarah, probably two of my favorite people in the world.

cues.zh: 而且，嗯，整整一年前的今天，他们在伊拉克库尔德斯坦徒步时，被伊朗军方绑架了。
cues.en: And, um, exactly one year ago today, they were hiking in Kurdistan, Iraq and were kidnapped by, uh, the Iranian military.

cues.zh: 过去这一年，他们一直被关在伊朗的监狱里。
cues.en: And for the past year they've been held in prison in Iran.

cues.zh: 嗯，Sarah 一直被单独监禁。
cues.en: Um, Sarah has been in solitary confinement.

cues.zh: 呃，而且似乎没有任何他们要获释的迹象。
cues.en: Uh, and there doesn't seem to be any sign of, uh, them being released.

cues.zh: 嗯，这种情况让人非常无力。
cues.en: Um, this it's a pretty disempowering situation.

cues.zh: 你知道，我或我认识的任何人都无能为力。
cues.en: You know, there's nothing that I or anyone that I know can do.

cues.zh: 但是，嗯，我一直想着他们，我只是想让其他人知道，你知道，有人被困在伊朗的监狱里，而且，呃，到今天正好一年了。
cues.en: But, um, I think about them all the time and I just want other people to know that, you know, people are stuck in prison in Iran and, uh, it's been exactly one year as of today.

cues.zh: 好的。
cues.en: All right.

cues.zh: 谢谢。
cues.en: Thanks.

cues.zh: 呃，好，我想花点时间谈谈隐私。
cues.en: Uh, okay, so, I would like to take some time to talk about privacy.

cues.zh: 嗯，我想先回顾一下过去。
cues.en: Um, what I'd like to do is start by looking into the past.

cues.zh: 呃，聊聊我们看到的威胁，以及我们认为重要的事情。
cues.en: Uh, talking about the threats that we saw, the things that we thought were important.

cues.zh: 呃，还有我们认为值得投入的项目。
cues.en: Uh, the projects that we thought were worth working on.

cues.zh: 然后我想稍微谈谈我觉得趋势是如何变化的，呃，再展望一下未来。
cues.en: And then I want to talk a little bit about how I feel like trends have changed and, uh, then look into the future.

cues.zh: 并稍微谈谈，呃，我认为接下来可能重要的事情。
cues.en: And talk a little bit about, uh, things that I think might be important moving forward.

cues.zh: 呃，我感兴趣去做的事情，也许其他人也会感兴趣去做的事情。
cues.en: Uh, things that I'm interested in working on and that maybe other people might be interested in working on.

cues.zh: 所以，回顾过去，90年代的技术叙事，呃，很大程度上被一个不好用的点击器所主导。
cues.en: So, looking into the past, the sort of technology narrative of the 90s, uh, was largely dominated by a clicker that doesn't work.

cues.zh: 呃，通过这个东西。
cues.en: Uh, by this thing.

cues.zh: 啊，我不打算用这个。
cues.en: Ah, I'm just not going to use this.

cues.zh: 网页浏览器。
cues.en: The web browser.

cues.zh: 呃，当网景首次推出Netscape Navigator时，那几乎是革命性的。
cues.en: Uh, when Netscape first introduced Netscape Navigator, it was almost revolutionary.

cues.zh: 而且，呃，很多人都想利用这一知识。
cues.en: And, uh, a lot of people moved to capitalize on that knowledge.

cues.zh: 呃，特别是，想要保护自身利益的主要参与者之一就是微软。
cues.en: Uh, in particular, one of the major players that wanted to protect their interests was Microsoft.

cues.zh: 而且，呃，当他们推出Internet Explorer时，叙事就变了，呃，从浏览器的概念，呃，变成了浏览器大战。
cues.en: And, uh, when they introduced Internet Explorer, the narrative changed, uh, just from, uh, the idea of a browser to, uh, this browser war.

cues.zh: 呃，在网景和Internet Explorer之间。
cues.en: Uh, between Netscape and Internet Explorer.

cues.zh: 我们都知道浏览器大战的结果如何。
cues.en: And we all know how the browser war's turned out.

cues.zh: 呃，但与此同时，还有另一场战争正在发生，它，嗯，某种程度上更微妙，但同样激烈，也许更为重要。
cues.en: Uh, but at the same time, there was there was another war that was happening and it was, um, somewhat more subtle, but it was just as fierce, and perhaps more important.

cues.zh: 而这场战争争夺的就是这个东西。
cues.en: And it was a war over this thing.

cues.zh: 呃，就是网页浏览器左下角那个小挂锁。
cues.en: Uh, the little padlock, uh, in the bottom left-hand corner of the web browser.

cues.zh: 更重要的是它背后的技术。
cues.en: And more importantly, the technology behind it.

cues.zh: 呃，这场战争的一方是密码朋克。
cues.en: Uh, on one side of this war, uh, were the cypherpunks.

cues.zh: 这些人希望让这类信息和技术广泛传播。
cues.en: These are people who wanted to see this information and technology spread widely.

cues.zh: 他们想把它推广到全世界，让许多人都能使用。
cues.en: They wanted to proliferate this throughout the world so that many people could use it.

cues.zh: 而这场战争的另一方是窃听者。
cues.en: And on the other side of this war, were the eavesdroppers.

cues.zh: 这些人想阻止这类信息传播，呃，并压制这项技术的使用。
cues.en: And these were people who wanted to prevent the spread of this information and, uh, stifle the use of this technology.

cues.zh: 于是，阵营就这样划开了。
cues.en: And so the lines were drawn.

cues.zh: 在密码朋克这一边，有像 Matt Blaze、呃、Philip Zimmerman、Ian Goldberg、David Chaum 和 Timothy May 这样的人。
cues.en: And on the Cypherpunk side, you had people like Matt Blaze, uh, Philip Zimmerman, Ian Goldberg, David Chaum and Timothy May.

cues.zh: 我青少年时代的英雄。
cues.en: The heroes of my teenage years.

cues.zh: 而那些监听者认为这些人很危险。
cues.en: And the eavesdroppers thought that these people were dangerous.

cues.zh: 事实上，他们的想法把那些人吓得要死。
cues.en: In fact, their ideas scared the fuck out of them.

cues.zh: 他们谈论的是这样一种转变：从一个他们能完全控制并完全获取所有信息的世界，转向一个他们既无法控制也无法获取任何信息的世界。
cues.en: They were talking about the move from a world where they had ultimate control and ultimate access to all information to a world where they would have no control and no access to any information.

cues.zh: 事实上，他们觉得这太危险了，以至于把这些想法列为武器。
cues.en: In fact, they thought this was so dangerous that they classified these ideas as weapons.

cues.zh: 如果你写了一点加密代码，发给加拿大的朋友，那就等同于出口军火，你可能因此被审判和起诉。
cues.en: That if you wrote a little bit of crypto code and sent it to your friend in Canada, that was tantamount to exporting munitions and you could be tried and prosecuted as such.

cues.zh: 但与此同时，他们也意识到，隐私这件事可能对某些人很重要，而且这个想法可能会流行起来。
cues.en: At the same time, however, they realized that, you know, this privacy thing might be important to some people and that, you know, this idea might catch on.

cues.zh: 于是，呃，他们决定搞出自己的解决方案，嗯，叫做密钥托管。
cues.en: And so, uh, they decided to come up with their own solution, um, which they called key escrow.

cues.zh: 而它最典型的体现，就是这个东西：Clipper 芯片。
cues.en: And, uh, was best embodied by this thing, the clipper chip.

cues.zh: 呃，他们想做的是制造这种芯片，然后把它嵌入每一件消费通信电子设备中。
cues.en: Uh, what they wanted to do was make this chip and then embed it into every piece of consumer communications electronics.

cues.zh: 每一部电话、每一台传真机、每一台个人电脑。
cues.en: Every telephone, every fax machine, every personal computer.

cues.zh: 而它的功能是，呃，做一些密码学运算。
cues.en: And what it would do is, uh, some cryptography.

cues.zh: 但它是个封闭系统，你没法接触到这块芯片的内部。
cues.en: But it was a a closed system and you wouldn't be able to get access to the internals of this chip.

cues.zh: 呃，你可以用它来，呃，发起安全会话。
cues.en: Uh, and you would be able to use it to, uh, start secure sessions.

cues.zh: 唯一的玄机在于，嗯，政府会拥有相当于一把主密钥的东西，然后就能用它解密任何他们认为可能有意思的内容。
cues.en: The only trick was that, um, the government would have like the equivalent of a master key which they could then use to decrypt anything that they thought might be interesting.

cues.zh: 这里窃听者的问题在于，嗯，密码学不是一根香蕉。
cues.en: So, the eavesdropper's problem here was that, um, cryptography is not a banana.

cues.zh: 也就是说，很难把信息当作对象来处理，对吧？
cues.en: Which is to say that it's difficult to treat information as objects, right?

cues.zh: 你知道，如果我有一根香蕉，把它给朋友、和朋友分享，嗯，世界上仍然只有一根香蕉。
cues.en: You know, if I have a banana and I give it, share it with my friend, um, there's still only one banana in the world.

cues.zh: 呃，然后他们再和朋友分享，世界上仍然只有一根香蕉。
cues.en: Uh, if they then share it with a friend of theirs, there's still only one banana in the world.

cues.zh: 呃，但信息不一样。
cues.en: Uh, however, information works differently.

cues.zh: 每次我分享信息，呃，其实都是在复制它，而且有可能出现指数级爆炸。
cues.en: Every time I share information, uh, I'm copying it and there's a chance for an exponential explosion.

cues.zh: 呃，这种根本困境，被一句密码朋克信条弄得更糟。
cues.en: Uh, this sort of fundamental dilemma was made worse by a cyber-punk mantra.

cues.zh: 密码朋克写代码。
cues.en: Cypherpunks write code.

cues.zh: 其想法是，学术界和研究界已经在政府领域之外做了大量出色工作，呃，开发公钥密码学，以及，呃，其他加密系统。
cues.en: The idea was that a lot of good work had been done in academia and research circles, uh, developing public key cryptography and, uh, other encryption systems outside the, the government realm.

cues.zh: 但是，呃，真正把它付诸实践的工作还做得不多。
cues.en: But, uh, not a lot had been done to actually put it into practice.

cues.zh: 而 Cypherpunks 想要的是人们能立刻下载并使用、进行安全通信的实际软件。
cues.en: And what Cypherpunks wanted were was actual software that people could download and use right now to communicate securely.

cues.zh: 于是他们有点疯了。
cues.en: And so they kind of went nuts.

cues.zh: 呃，有些人搬到了安圭拉，呃，那是加勒比海的一座岛，在密码学出口方面有非常有利的法律，他们开始编写加密代码，并试图把它分发到全世界。
cues.en: Uh, some people moved to Anguilla, uh, an island in the Caribbean that had very favorable laws in terms of exporting cryptography and started writing crypto code and trying to ship it throughout the world.

cues.zh: 嗯，还有更有创意的策略，比如在，呃，1995 年，呃，Philip Zimmerman 与 MIT Press 合作出版了一本书，呃，叫《PGP: Source Code and Internals》。
cues.en: Um, there were more creative strategies like in, uh, 1995, uh, Philip Zimmerman published a book, uh, in conjunction with MIT press called PGP: Source Code and Internals.

cues.zh: 而关键在于，呃，这本书其实就是把完整的 PGP 源代码用机器可读的字体印了出来。
cues.en: And the deal was that, uh, the book was just the entire PGP source code printed in a machine-readable font.

cues.zh: 因为，你知道，密码学的数字形式算是武器，可一旦印在书里，那就是言论。
cues.en: Um, because, you know, digital representations of cryptography were weapons, but if you printed it in a book, that was speech.

cues.zh: 于是他们把整本书印了出来，印量很小，然后，呃，就把它分发到全世界每个想看到它的国家。
cues.en: Uh, so they printed this whole thing in a book and the very small print run, and then, uh, you know, just shifted to every country in the world where they wanted to see this.

cues.zh: 接着人们又把它扫描回电脑里，因为那是机器可读的字体。
cues.en: And then people just scanned it back in because it was a machine-readable font.

cues.zh: 于是 PGP 就这样完全合法地传遍了全世界。
cues.en: And now, uh, PGP had been distributed completely legally all over the world.

cues.zh: 所以这类事一直在继续，策略越来越快，密码学也越来越普及，直到 2000 年，克林顿政府突然废除了所有限制密码学出口的重要法律。
cues.en: So, you know, this kind of stuff continued and I mean the strategies got more and more rapid and uh cryptography became more and more ubiquitous, um, until 2000, when suddenly the Clinton administration repealed all of the significant laws limiting the export of cryptography.

cues.zh: 于是，看起来游戏已经结束，世界已经被赢下了。
cues.en: And so it sort of seemed like the game was over, that the the world was won.

cues.zh: 如果你回过头，看看，呃，密码朋克关于密码学一旦无处不在会发生什么的预测。
cues.en: If you go back and you look at, uh, the cypherpunk predictions about what would happen once cryptography was ubiquitous.

cues.zh: 呃，他们做出的第一个预测很简单：它会变得无处不在，会不可避免地，呃，传遍全世界。
cues.en: Uh, the, the first prediction, uh, uh, that they made was simply that it would become ubiquitous that it would inevitably, uh, spread throughout the world.

cues.zh: 而这结果成了他们最有先见之明的预测。
cues.en: And this turned out to be their most prescient prediction.

cues.zh: 这真的是我们最早几次看到信息确实想要自由。
cues.en: This is really one of the first times that we saw that information really does want to be free.

cues.zh: 但如果你看看，嗯，他们对一旦它无处不在会发生什么的预测，这些就没那么有先见之明了。
cues.en: But if you you look at, um, their predictions of what would happen once it was ubiquitous, they were somewhat less prescient.

cues.zh: 嗯，匿名数字货币会繁荣，知识产权会消失，监控会变得不可能。
cues.en: Um, that anonymous digital cash would flourish, that intellectual property would disappear, that surveillance would become impossible.

cues.zh: 呃，那样政府就无法继续征税，政府会垮台。
cues.en: Uh, that governments would then be unable to continue collecting taxes and that governments would fall.

cues.zh: 如果从这些预测作出时快进 10 年。
cues.en: If you flash forward 10 years from when these predictions were made.

cues.zh: 嗯，密码学让你能安全地把信用卡号传给 amazon.com，好买一本 Sarah Palin 的《Going Rogue》。
cues.en: Um, cryptography is the thing that allows you to securely transmit your credit card number to amazon.com so you can buy a copy of Sarah Palin's book on Going Rogue.

cues.zh: 你知道，当然，其中一些，呃，想法多少被削弱了。
cues.en: You know, sure, some of these, um, ideas have been eroded somewhat.

cues.zh: 嗯，但监控大概处于历史最高点，而隐私大概处于历史最低点。
cues.en: Um, but surveillance is probably at an all-time high while privacy is probably at an all-time low.

cues.zh: 那发生了什么？
cues.en: So what happened?

cues.zh: 你知道，感觉我们像是在打这场仗，而且好像赢了，可现在却处于这种奇怪的境地。
cues.en: You know, it sort of seemed like we were waging this war and it seemed like we won the war and, and now here we are in this strange situation.

cues.zh: 嗯，我觉得，呃，我的部分论点是，呃，在很多方面，我感觉密码朋克是在为未来做准备。
cues.en: Well, I think, uh, part of my thesis here is that, uh, in many ways, I feel like the cypherpunks were preparing for a future.

cues.zh: 呃，他们预想的未来是法西斯主义。
cues.en: Uh, and the future that they anticipated was fascism.

cues.zh: 但我们得到的是社会民主主义。
cues.en: But what we got was social democracy.

cues.zh: 而这未必更好。
cues.en: And that's not necessarily better.

cues.zh: 只是不一样。
cues.en: It's just different.

cues.zh: 嗯，我举个例子。
cues.en: Um, let me give you an example.

cues.zh: 在座有多少人会乐意接受这样一条法律：要求每个人随时随地携带政府强制配备的追踪设备？
cues.en: How many people in this room would feel good about a law which required everyone to carry a government-mandated tracking device with them at all times?

cues.zh: 对，没有，一个人都没有。
cues.en: Yeah, no, not even one person.

cues.zh: 好吧。
cues.en: All right.

cues.zh: 所以那，那就是法西斯主义，对吧？
cues.en: So that's that's fascism, right?

cues.zh: 那就是法西斯式的未来。
cues.en: That's the fascist future.

cues.zh: 嗯，现在我再问一个问题。
cues.en: Um, now let me ask another question.

cues.zh: 在座有多少人，呃，带手机？
cues.en: How many people here, uh, carry a mobile phone?

cues.zh: 对吧。
cues.en: Right.

cues.zh: 我，我猜实际上在座 100% 的人都带。
cues.en: I I'm guessing actually 100% of the people in this room.

cues.zh: 嗯，所以那就是社会民主主义，对吧？
cues.en: Um, and so that's social democracy, right?

cues.zh: 因为政府强制配备的追踪设备和手机到底有什么区别，你知道吗？
cues.en: Cuz so what is the difference between a government-mandated tracking device and a mobile phone, you know?

cues.zh: 手机不过就是个追踪设备，嗯，把你的实时位置报告给少数几家电信公司之一，而法律要求这些公司把信息交给政府。
cues.en: A mobile phone is just, uh, a tracking device that reports your real-time position to, uh, one of a few telecommunications companies which are required by law to turn that information over to the government.

cues.zh: 所以从实际操作上说，它们是一样的，你懂吧？
cues.en: So logistically, they're the same, you know?

cues.zh: 嗯，那区别是什么？
cues.en: Um, so what is the difference?

cues.zh: 关掉它。
cues.en: Turn it off.

cues.zh: 你可以关掉它，但你没关。
cues.en: You can turn it off, but you don't.

cues.zh: 有时候吧。
cues.en: Sometimes.

cues.zh: 心理上的。
cues.en: Psychological.

cues.zh: 你自己就在这么做。
cues.en: You're doing it.

cues.zh: 选择。
cues.en: Choice.

cues.zh: 而且手机是你花钱买的。
cues.en: And you pay for one.

cues.zh: 嗯，对。
cues.en: Uh, yeah.

cues.zh: 选择，对吧？
cues.en: Choice, right?

cues.zh: 选择就是最大的区别，你懂吧？
cues.en: Choice is the big difference, you know?

cues.zh: 你选择随身带手机，嗯，而你不会选择随身带这个政府强制配发的追踪设备。
cues.en: You choose to carry a cell phone, uh, and you you wouldn't choose to carry this government-mandated tracking device.

cues.zh: 嗯，那我们来聊聊这个，你懂吧？
cues.en: Um, so let's talk about that, you know?

cues.zh: 我做梦也没想到自己会有手机。
cues.en: Never in my wildest dreams did I think that I would have a cell phone.

cues.zh: 我怎么会呢，你懂吧？
cues.en: Why would I, you know?

cues.zh: 它是个移动追踪设备，是个移动窃听器，运行在不安全的协议上。
cues.en: It's a mobile tracking device, it's a mobile bug, it operates over an insecure protocol.

cues.zh: 我为什么会想要这种东西？
cues.en: Why would I want one of these things?

cues.zh: 呃，可我还真有一个。
cues.en: Uh, and yet I have one.

cues.zh: 而且我每天都随身带着它。
cues.en: And I carry it with me all the time, every day.

cues.zh: 嗯，我觉得如果看看人们在群体中沟通和协调的方式，呃，通常他们用的是一些非正式的、呃，机制和渠道，用来，呃，沟通、呃，做计划、保持联系。
cues.en: Well, I think if we look at the way that people tend to communicate and coordinate in groups, uh, often they are sort of informal, uh, mechanisms and channels that people use to, uh, communicate and to, uh, make plans and stay in touch.

cues.zh: 而如果我引入一种更规范的通信渠道，就会遇到一个众所周知的问题，叫无网络效应：呃，我发明了这东西，也许像 GSM 蜂窝网络，我开始用它，但它很难用，因为网络的价值在于连接到它的节点数量。
cues.en: And if I introduce a more codified communications channel, there's a well-known problem called the no-network effect where, uh, I invent this thing, maybe like the GSM cellular network, and I start using it, but it's difficult to use because the value of that network is in the number of nodes that are connected to it.

cues.zh: 如果只有我一个人用它，那它其实没多大价值。
cues.en: And if I'm the only one using it, then it's really not worth very much.

cues.zh: 但如果我能设法让所有人都开始用这个东西，它就变得非常有用、非常有价值。
cues.en: If, however, I somehow manage to get everyone, uh, to start using this thing, then it becomes very useful and very valuable.

cues.zh: 但这有个有趣的副作用，就是旧的、那些非正式的沟通和协调方式被摧毁了。
cues.en: Uh, but there's there's an interesting side effect, which is that the old, uh, informal methods of communication and coordination are destroyed.

cues.zh: 技术实际上改变了社会的结构。
cues.en: That technology actually changes the fabric of society.

cues.zh: 我是说，在手机领域，这种琐碎或老套的例子有很多，对吧？
cues.en: Uh, I mean, there are many sort of trivial or trite examples of this, uh, in the mobile phone, uh, world, right?

cues.zh: 我们看到手机改变了人们做计划的方式，对吧？
cues.en: Where, you know, we see that mobile phones have changed the way that people make plans, right?

cues.zh: 以前人们做计划时会说："我们在这个时间在街角碰头，然后一起去那个活动。"
cues.en: It used to be that people made plans, you know, they'd say, "I'll meet you on the street corner at this time and we'll go to this thing."

cues.zh: 现在人们会说：“我下班的时候给你打电话。”
cues.en: And now people say, "I'll call you when I'm getting off work."

cues.zh: 所以，如果你没有那项技术，你就无法以社会沟通和协作的方式参与其中。
cues.en: And so, if you don't have the, uh, that piece of technology, uh, you can't participate in the way that, uh, society is communicating and coordinating.

cues.zh: 于是实际发生的情况是：如果我现在决定不想参与这个被编码化的沟通渠道，我就又一次成了“无网络效应”的受害者。
cues.en: Uh, and so what actually ends up happening is now if I decide that I don't want to participate in this codified communication channel, I'm once again victim to the no-network effect.

cues.zh: 因为我想做的是加入一个已经被摧毁的网络。
cues.en: Because what I'm trying to do is go be a part of a network that has been destroyed.

cues.zh: 它不再存在了，而我又一次成了唯一使用它的人，我身处一个几乎没有价值的网络之中。
cues.en: Um, that no longer exists and I'm once again the only one using it, uh, and I'm part of a network that has very little value.

cues.zh: 所以没错，我做了选择，对吧？
cues.en: So yes, I made a choice, right?

cues.zh: 选择拥有一部手机。
cues.en: To have a cell phone.

cues.zh: 但我做的究竟是什么样的选择呢？
cues.en: But what kind of choice did I make?

cues.zh: 嗯，我觉得现在事情往往就是这样发展的。
cues.en: Um, and I I think that this is the way that things tend to go now.

cues.zh: 最终发生的情况是，这些选择起初非常简单。
cues.en: That what ends up happening is the choices start out very simple.

cues.zh: 呃，“我口袋里到底有没有一件计算消费电子产品？”
cues.en: Uh, "Do I have a compute piece of consumer electronics in my pocket or not?"

cues.zh: 随着时间的推移，这个选择的范围慢慢扩大，直到它变成了一个是否参与社会的选择。
cues.en: And over time, the scope of that choice slowly expands until it becomes a choice to participate in society or not.

cues.zh: 在今天的某种程度上，选择不拥有手机，在某种意义上就意味着选择不参与社会。
cues.en: That on some level today, to choose not to have a cell phone means, in some sense, to choose not to participate in society.

cues.zh: 所以我认为，如果我们开始审视这种小选择变成大选择的模式，你就会发现它们无处不在。
cues.en: And so I think if we start looking at this pattern of small choices becoming big choices, you start to see them everywhere.

cues.zh: 呃，我最喜欢、最新的例子之一，来自这个叫 Adblock Plus 的 Firefox 扩展。
cues.en: Uh, one of my favorite, most recent examples is, uh, from this Firefox extension called Adblock Plus.

cues.zh: 我相信很多人都熟悉这个。
cues.en: I'm sure that many people are familiar with this.

cues.zh: 它的理念是帮助你屏蔽网络上的广告。
cues.en: The idea is that it's supposed to help you block ads on the web.

cues.zh: 它的原理是，让你指定，嗯，一组正则表达式，呃，用来匹配你的 URL，也就是广告 URL。
cues.en: And the way it works is it allows you to specify, um, a set of regular expressions, uh, that would match your URLs, that would be advertising URLs.

cues.zh: 呃，用于广告横幅之类的东西。
cues.en: Uh, for ad banners and stuff like that.

cues.zh: 而且，嗯，问题在于，你知道，这挺有效的，但这些 URL 一直在变。
cues.en: And, um, the problem with this is, you know, it's quite effective, but these URLs are constantly changing.

cues.zh: 所以你也得不断修改你的正则表达式。
cues.en: And so you want to be changing your regular expressions as well.

cues.zh: 而要跟上这种变化可能会挺麻烦的。
cues.en: And it's could be kind of a pain to try and keep up with that.

cues.zh: 所以他们做了个聪明的设计，采用订阅模式。
cues.en: So they've done a clever thing where they have a subscription model.

cues.zh: 也就是说，你可以订阅一份别人维护的正则表达式列表。
cues.en: Where what you can do is you can subscribe to a list of regular expressions that someone else is maintaining.

cues.zh: 呃，这样一来，你知道，你只需要一个人或一组人，比较敏锐、跟得上变化。
cues.en: Uh, that way, you know, you only need one person or a group of people who are sort of on the ball.

cues.zh: 呃，来研究这些正则表达式，其他人就只是，呃，从这项研究中受益。
cues.en: Uh, looking at these regular expressions and everyone else just benefits, uh, from, uh, that research.

cues.zh: 而且，嗯，现在，呃，有不少流行的订阅列表，它们并不都是为了，嗯，广告，对吧？
cues.en: And, um, now, uh, so there's a number of popular subscriptions and they're not all for, um, ads, right?

cues.zh: 所以有一些流行的订阅列表，是用来拦截跟踪器的。
cues.en: So there's a few popular subscriptions for blocking trackers.

cues.zh: 你知道，它们就像网络臭虫，会在你浏览网页时跟踪你的行踪。
cues.en: You know, these are like web bugs that track your movements around the web as you browse along.

cues.zh: 所以我就订阅了其中一个跟踪器列表。
cues.en: And so I'm subscribed to one of these tracker lists.

cues.zh: 而且，呃，当然，我最想拦截的跟踪器之一就是 Google Analytics。
cues.en: And, uh, of course, one of the trackers that I'm most interested in blocking is Google Analytics.

cues.zh: 呃，因为，你知道，Google Analytics 完全没问题。
cues.en: Uh, because, you know, there's no problem with Google Analytics at all.

cues.zh: 然后有一天，发生了件有趣的事。
cues.en: And one day, something interesting happened.

cues.zh: 呃，Google Analytics 从我订阅的，呃，跟踪器列表里消失了。
cues.en: Uh, Google Analytics disappeared from the list of, uh, trackers in my subscription.

cues.zh: 你知道，如果你想想过去那个世界，事情以前的运作方式，你会想象某个 Google 高管追查到维护这个列表的人，然后，你知道，用一箱现金让他闭嘴，还搞了什么见不得光的幕后交易。
cues.en: And, you know, if you think about the old world, the way that things used to work, you imagine that some Google executive tracked down the person who's maintaining this list and, you know, shut up with a briefcase full of cash and there was some shady backroom deal.

cues.zh: 在大家握手之后，你知道，呃，Google Analytics 就被从这份名单里移除了。
cues.en: Where hands were shaken and, you know, uh, Google Analytics was removed from this list.

cues.zh: 据我所知，事情并不是那样；实际发生的要微妙得多，也阴险得多。
cues.en: As far as I can tell, that's not what happened and that actually something much more subtle and much more insidious actually happened.

cues.zh: 呃，Google Analytics 的工作方式，嗯，是通过 JavaScript。
cues.en: Uh, the way that Google Analytics works is, um, through JavaScript.

cues.zh: 呃，情况是这样的，呃，想用 Google Analytics 的网站运营者，只需把一小段 JavaScript 引入他们的 HTML 文件。
cues.en: Uh, what happens is, uh, website operators who wish to use Google Analytics, just import a little bit of JavaScript into their HTML file.

cues.zh: 而且，呃，页面加载时，这段 JavaScript 就会跟踪你。
cues.en: And, uh, when the page loads, the JavaScript tracks you.

cues.zh: 现在，呃，Google 的做法是，开始把一些小型、通用且实用的 JavaScript 函数，加入这个 Google Analytics 的 JavaScript 文件。
cues.en: Now, uh, what Google did was they started including small bits of just usefully generic JavaScript functions into this Google Analytics JavaScript file.

cues.zh: 他们本质上是在说：“嘿，你们反正都要为了在网站上用 Google Analytics 而引入这个 JavaScript 文件。
cues.en: And what they were essentially saying was, "Hey, you guys are importing this JavaScript file anyway just to use Google Analytics on your website.

cues.zh: 我们会附带加入几个通用工具函数，而且我们做得很到位，你知道，我们想清楚了。
cues.en: We're going to throw in a few just generically useful functions, and we've done this right and, you know, we figure this out.

cues.zh: 只要你导入了这个东西，就可以使用它们。
cues.en: That you can use as long as you're importing this thing.

cues.zh: 这样一来，你就能直接把它用于网站的核心功能。
cues.en: And that way, you can just use it for the, the core functionality of your website."

cues.zh: 所以现在的情况是，如果你屏蔽 Google Analytics 的 JavaScript，你不仅会搞坏 Google Analytics，实际上还会破坏网站的核心功能。
cues.en: And so now, what happens is if you block the Google Analytics JavaScript, you don't just break Google Analytics, you actually break the core functionality of the website.

cues.zh: 因为现在这个 JavaScript 里，网站实际依赖其实现功能的那些 JavaScript 函数已经不存在了。
cues.en: Because now this JavaScript, JavaScript functions the website is actually depending on for the functionality of the website don't exist.

cues.zh: 所以，再说一次，他们所做的就是扩大了你必须做出选择的范围。
cues.en: And so, again, what they've done is they've expanded the scope of the choice that you have to make.

cues.zh: 这原本只是一个非常简单的小选择。
cues.en: This used to be a very simple small choice.

cues.zh: 我想不想被 Google 追踪？
cues.en: Do I want to be tracked by Google or not?

cues.zh: 很简单，要么屏蔽 JavaScript，要么不屏蔽。
cues.en: Simple enough, you can either block the JavaScript or not block the JavaScript.

cues.zh: 现在，选择变多了。
cues.en: Now, the choice becomes larger.

cues.zh: 我要不要访问这个网站？
cues.en: Do I want to visit this website or not?

cues.zh: 同样，这个选择要难得多。
cues.en: And again, that's a much more difficult choice to make.

cues.zh: 那么，这为什么重要？
cues.en: So, you know, why is this significant?

cues.zh: 对吧？
cues.en: Right?

cues.zh: 嗯，好吧。
cues.en: Um, well, okay.

cues.zh: 这个人叫 John Poindexter。
cues.en: This guy's name is John Poindexter.

cues.zh: 顺便说，他被认定对 Iran-Contra 丑闻负最大责任。
cues.en: Uh, and then, he's incidentally the guy who is found to be most responsible for the Iran Contra scandal.

cues.zh: 他因向国会作伪证被定罪，但后来从未入狱。
cues.en: He was, uh, convicted of lying to Congress, but then never went to jail.

cues.zh: 2001 年，他启动了一个政府项目，叫 Total Information Awareness。
cues.en: Um, and in 2001, he started a program, a government program called Total Information Awareness.

cues.zh: 他在宣布该项目时发表演讲说，数据必须放入大型存储库，并带有增强的语义内容，以便于分析。
cues.en: And, uh, he, he made a speech, uh, when he announced the program where he said that data must be made available in large-scale repositories with enhanced semantic content for easy analysis.

cues.zh: 本质上，他想做的是让政府截取所有电子邮件流量、所有网络流量、所有信用卡记录，以及每个人的医疗记录。
cues.en: And essentially what he wanted to do was have the government siphon off all email traffic, all web traffic, all credit card history, everybody's medical records.

cues.zh: 呃，然后全扔进一个大数据池里。
cues.en: Uh, and throw it into one big sink.

cues.zh: 就是先堆成一大堆。不用操心分析，也不用实时处理。
cues.en: Just put it in one big pile. Don't worry about analyzing it or processing it processing it in real time.

cues.zh: 呃，然后再开发出能真正高效挖掘这些数据的技术，呃，来提取他们未来任何时候感兴趣的那些统计、关系和画像。
cues.en: Uh, and then develop the, um, technology to really efficiently mine this data, uh, to pull out the interesting statistics, relationships, profiles, uh, that they were interested in at any point in the future.

cues.zh: 所以你只要收集这一大池子数据，然后，呃，未来任何时候都可以回头从中取出任何你想要的东西。
cues.en: So you just collect this big sink of data, and then, uh, at any point in the future, you can go back and pull out anything that you want from it.

cues.zh: 呃，所以这就是那个极权未来。
cues.en: Uh, so this was the totalitarian future.

cues.zh: 这就是，呃，密码朋克一直担心的那个噩梦，你知道，对吧？
cues.en: This was the, the cypherpunk nightmare that, you know, they had been worried about, right?

cues.zh: 这就是他们一直以来思考和准备的东西。
cues.en: This is what they had been thinking about and preparing for all this time.

cues.zh: 人们吓坏了。
cues.en: And people freaked out.

cues.zh: 我是说，你知道，这是新闻里的一件大事。
cues.en: I mean, you know, this was, um, the, you know, a significant story in the news.

cues.zh: 呃，人们群情激愤，事实上，连国会都问：“你们到底在干什么？”你知道。
cues.en: Uh, people were up in arms, and in fact, even Congress was like, "What are you guys doing?" you know.

cues.zh: 呃，最终这个项目被关停了。
cues.en: Uh, and eventually the program was shut down.

cues.zh: 好吧。
cues.en: Well, okay.

cues.zh: 那为什么被关停了呢？
cues.en: So why was it shut down?

cues.zh: 你知道，首先，这些人显然来自旧世界。
cues.en: You know, first of all, these people are clearly from the old world.

cues.zh: 他们根本不知道自己在干什么。
cues.en: They really don't know what they're doing.

cues.zh: 这是他们实际用的标志。
cues.en: This was their actual logo.

cues.zh: 这不是 The Onion 仿照这个做的恶搞标志。这是他们自己设计出来的标志。
cues.en: This isn't like the Onion made a logo in parody of this. This was the logo they came up with.

cues.zh: 他们有金字塔、上帝之眼，还有一道光束照向地球。
cues.en: They have the pyramid with the eye of God and a light beam shining down on the planet.

cues.zh: 下面那点拉丁文的意思是“知识就是力量”。
cues.en: That little bit of Latin under there means knowledge is power.

cues.zh: 我是说，拜托，你知道的。
cues.en: I mean, come on, you know.

cues.zh: 我是说，如果你要搞个吓人的政府项目，你知道，你得有个友好的标志。
cues.en: I mean, if you're going to have some like scary government program, you know, you need like a friendly logo.

cues.zh: 你知道，别，你知道，别叫它 Total Information Awareness。
cues.en: You know, don't, you know, don't call it Total Information Awareness.

cues.zh: 叫它小猫监控协会之类的，你知道吧？
cues.en: Call it the Kitten Surveillance Society or something, you know?

cues.zh: 我是说，真的，你得弄点色彩鲜艳的、你知道、几乎卡通化的东西，看起来幼稚，而且而且而且完全无害，你知道。
cues.en: I mean, I mean, really, you want something that's sort of like colorful, you know, almost cartoonish, something that seems childish and and and really harmless, you know.

cues.zh: 呃，差不多这样的东西。
cues.en: Uh, something like this.

cues.zh: 因为如果你回头看看 Total Information Awareness 当初想做什么，Google 全做了。
cues.en: Cuz if you go back and you look at what Total Information Awareness was trying to do, Google has done all of it.

cues.zh: 呃，我是说，事实上。
cues.en: Uh, I mean, in fact.

cues.zh: 他们已经超出了 TIA 原本设想收集和处理的范围。
cues.en: They have exceeded the original scope of what TIA dreamed to collect and process.

cues.zh: 呃，而且我们知道他们真正擅长的一件事，嗯，其实也是他们赚钱的方式，就是能够非常高效地，呃，挖掘他们收集的数据。
cues.en: Uh, and one thing that we know that they've really excelled at, um, and and actually how they've made their money, is in being able to really efficiently, uh, mine the data that they collect.

cues.zh: 嗯，提取出他们未来任何时候可能感兴趣的有趣统计数据、关系和用户画像等等。
cues.en: Uh, to pull out the interesting statistics, relationships, profiles, uh, that they were interested in at any point in the future.

cues.en: So you just collect this big sink of data, and then, uh, and at any point in the future you can go back and pull out anything that you want from it.

cues.en: Uh, so this was the totalitarian future.

cues.en: This is what they had been thinking about and preparing for all this time.

cues.en: And people freaked out.

cues.en: I mean, you know, this was, um, the, you know, a significant story in the news.

cues.zh: 嗯，人们群情激愤，事实上，连国会都说：“你们在干什么？”你知道。

cues.en: They really don't know what they're doing.

cues.en: This was their actual logo.

cues.zh: 这可不是《洋葱新闻》恶搞做的标志，这就是他们自己想出来的标志。
cues.en: This isn't like the Onion made a logo in parody of this. This was the logo they came up with.

cues.en: They have the pyramid with the eye of God and a light beam shining down on the planet.
